name: Pilocytic Astrocytoma with Histological Features of Anaplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Presence of increased mitotic activity, nuclear atypia, and necrosis on histopathology
Classic pilocytic astrocytoma features including biphasic pattern, Rosenthal fibers, and eosinophilic granular bodies
MRI showing cystic lesion with enhancing mural nodule typically in cerebellum or optic pathway

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histological confirmation of pilocytic astrocytoma with evidence of anaplasia (mitotic activity, nuclear atypia, or necrosis) with supportive imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing for BRAF alterations may assist but is not mandatory for diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal neurological deficits correlating with tumor location

common.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting secondary to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: vomiting caused by increased intracranial pressure
vision problems like double or blurry vision
walking difficulties and bladder control issues
symptoms from fluid buildup in brain
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor

rare.symptomName: Spinal cord compression symptoms if dissemination occurs
searchTerms: weakness or numbness from spine issues

laboratory: CSF analysis typically non-specific; may show mild protein elevation
imaging: MRI showing cystic mass with enhancing mural nodule, often in cerebellum or optic pathway
Possible evidence of tumor infiltration or necrosis in anaplastic areas
genetic: Frequent BRAF-KIAA1549 fusion in pilocytic astrocytoma component
Additional genetic alterations associated with anaplasia such as TP53 mutations may be present
other: Histopathology demonstrating biphasic pattern with Rosenthal fibers and eosinophilic granular bodies alongside anaplastic features

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of classic pilocytic features such as Rosenthal fibers
Lack of cystic architecture with mural nodule
More diffuse infiltration without biphasic pattern

redFlags: New onset seizures in a patient with known pilocytic astrocytoma
Signs of increased intracranial pressure refractory to treatment
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021.
Perry A, et al. Anaplastic transformation in pilocytic astrocytoma: a clinicopathologic study. Am J Surg Pathol. 2014.
